summary: Episodes 29-61 adapt Acts 50-148 (vols 7-17) of the Kyoto arc almost linearly and with no filler: animefillerlist and animefillerguide both type all of 28-62 as manga canon. The only structural non-linearity is a swap at eps 43/44: the anime runs Kenshin's ogi training (Acts 94-96) BEFORE Sano/Saito/Cho in the Kyoto jail (Acts 92-93), then resumes with Act 97; ep 43 also moves Act 95's childhood-massacre flashback to its cold open. Several episode breaks fall mid-chapter (Acts 119, 121, 130, 133, 146), recorded as continue points. Two sources were used for every anchor: animefillerguide's per-episode chapter table (verified from the raw HTML) and kenshin.fandom's chapter pages, whose '1996ep' field gives the reverse mapping for Acts 48-130; for Acts 131-151 the wiki has no 1996 field, so eps 55-61 rest on AFG plus content/title correlation (Wikipedia chapter titles, Japanese act titles, episode plot summaries). Surprises: the wiki tags Act 87 as Episode 44 (its content is ep 42's cold open), AFG's ep 48 cell is a typo ('110, 111, 110'), and the existing ep 28 anchor (48) is wrong - ep 28 ends on Act 49.

AFG and wiki both 72-73 ('Encounter in the Forest' I-II = Sano meets Anji and learns the Futae no Kiwami).
AFG and wiki both 74-77: 'Arrival in Kyoto' (74) through 'Prelude to Battle' (77) - Cho takes Iori, Kenshin waits at the Hakusan shrine.

AFG 87, 89-91 (88 omitted); wiki 89-91 -> Episode 42. Act 87 'Meeting of the Warlords' (Oniwabanshu flashback + Aoshi joins Shishio) is the cold open and the episode's title event - the wiki's '1996ep = Episode 44' on Act 87 is an error. AFG 98-101; wiki 98-101 -> Episode 45; title = Act 99 'As If in Flight' (Tobu ga Gotoku). Ends with the Rengoku revealed at Osaka harbour (101).
AFG 101-105 (101 = tail); wiki 102-105 -> Episode 46. Rengoku sunk (102), aftermath, rooftop night with Kaoru and dawn departure (105 'A Beautiful Night').
AFG 105-109 (105 = tail); wiki 106-109 -> Episode 47. Hoji's atonement (106) through Sano vs Anji until Anji rises again with the ihai (109 'Conviction of the Fist').
Wiki 110-111 -> Episode 48; AFG's cell reads '110, 111, 110' (typo). Anji's backstory (110) and the finish (111); the closing Usui-in-the-dark teaser is Act 112's opening, re-covered by ep 49.
AFG and wiki both 112-115: Saito vs Usui (113-114, Gatotsu Zeroshiki) and the Aoiya battle plan (115 'The Time Is Now'). Closing Aoshi-in-Hoji's-room teaser = Act 115's last page / 116's opening.
AFG 115-119; wiki 116-119 -> Episode 50. Ends mid-Act 119 right after Kenshin's Ryu Tsui Sen lands and Yumi's telegraph is exposed; the 'wake up' climax (rest of 119) opens ep 51.

AFG 119-121; wiki 120 -> Episode 51, 121 -> Episode 52. Episode title 'Mezameru toki wa ima' is Act 119's Japanese title (the wake-up shout); Amakakeru vs Kaiten Kenbu Rokuren = Act 120 ('Amakakeru Ryu no Hirameki sono ichi'). Closes on the first pages of 121 (Kamatari unmasked, Henya takes to the air); the bulk of 121 is ep 52, hence continue point 121.

AFG 122-124; wiki Act 121 -> Episode 52 plus 122-124. Episode title 'Aoiya no kobo' = Act 121's Japanese title 'Kobo Aoiya'. Yahiko vs Henya (121-122), Kaoru+Misao vs Kamatari (123), Fuji's shadow (124 'The Shadow of Despair').

AFG 125-128 (128 = the Sojiro-door teaser, re-covered at ep 54's open); wiki 125-127 -> Episode 53. Hiko descends (125), 'The Great Man vs. The Giant' I-II (126-127) = episode title 'Kyojin tai chojin' and vol 15's title.

AFG and wiki both 128-130. Sojiro's Shukuchi (129 = episode title), then the sandal-break pause inside Act 130 as Sojiro begins recalling his past; the flashback proper is ep 55, hence continue point 130. Sojiro killing Senkaku at the river is anime-original.

AFG 130-133 (wiki has no 1996 field from Act 131 on). 'Sojiro's Story' = Acts 130-132 (Moonlight Encounter, Feast of Thunder, Smile in the Freezing Rain - the stormy-night massacre of the episode title); the duel resumes into Act 133, whose breakdown proper ('Destruction of the Soul') opens ep 56, hence continue point 133.

AFG 133-135. Act 134 = Shuntensatsu vs Amakakeru (episode subtitle), Act 135 'Those Who Gather, Those Who Part' = Sojiro leaves, Yumi escorts Kenshin to the arena; ep 57's opening reflection is Act 136's title 'When Did the Battle Begin?'.
AFG 136-137. Act 136 'When Did the Battle Begin?' = Kenshin's stair-climb reflection; Act 137 'Fuel' = petroleum arena and the human-oil Mugenjin; Saito is absent (he joins in Act 138 = ep 58).
AFG 138-139. Guren Kaina, Saito and Sano join (Act 138 cast adds Saito), Shishio's 'Howling Laugh' (139) as Aoshi walks in (139 cast adds Aoshi) - the episode's closing beat.

AFG 140-142. Aoshi vs Shishio and Kenshin rising (140 'Thread of Life'), the comeback (141 'Double-Edged Flame'), Kaguzuchi readied (142 'Final Encounter'); ep 60 opens on Amakakeru vs Kaguzuchi = Act 143 'The Third Secret'.

AFG 143-146. Kaguzuchi vs Amakakeru (143), Yumi's death (144 'Shape of Love'), Shishio's combustion (145 'Duel of an Era'), Hoji's rampage begins (146 'The Passion of Hoji'); Act 146's escape half opens ep 61, hence continue point 146.

AFG 146-148. Escape from the burning base (146), one month later and Cho's report on the Juppongatana (147-148: Hoji's suicide omitted, Yumi's past, Sojiro's journey), Shishio in Hell closes 148. Ep 62 = 149-151 (existing anchor confirmed by AFG and MangaShed).

repairs.why: ep 28 adapts Acts 48-49: the wiki's Act 49 page is tagged 1996ep = Episode 28 and its 'differences' note (Megumi joining after the Akabeko meal) is the same scene the Episode 28 page describes; AFG lists 48, 49. Ep 29 begins on May 7 (Act 50 'Scheme'). Suggested chapters_adapted '48-49', start 48, vol 7.

structure.notes: Single TV component (AniList 45): AniList and MAL count 94 broadcast episodes (Fuji TV, 1996-01-10 to 1998-09-08); Wikipedia counts 95 because ep 95 'End of Wanderings' (1998-12-02) was a home-video-only bonus, which AniList catalogues separately as OVA 12067 'Rurou no Saihate'; kenshin.fandom has Episode pages only through 95. Our DB carries 100 rows for this component, so rows 95-100 do not follow the TV series' own numbering - worth a stitch check (possibly the 1997 specials 4664/9716 or the pilot-one-shot annotations). Kyoto arc = eps 28-62 <-> Acts 48-151 (vols 7-18) per the fandom Kyoto Arc page; everything from ep 63 on is anime-original. Cumulative numbering in this deliverable equals the TV numbering (AFG's season-2 numbers 01-35 map to 28-62).
